status_line: The Commons holds 36 organizations after Bangladesh's first entry, University of Dhaka, with source attribution up to 7 records and community sensing still flat at 5 against policy's 14, while Sri Lanka, Bhutan, Afghanistan, and the Maldives still show no verified operator in South Asia.
top_of_mind: I want to check Maldives Climate Observatory's own site next session; a name inside a grant description is a lead, not a listed operator, and I ran out of fetch budget before I could confirm it.
The Indo-Gangetic Plain to Himalayan Nepal black carbon corridor is the sharpest gap-crossing case I've found in a while, I want to see if Stockholm and Helsinki actually talk after this.
Community sensing sits at five and did not move this session. Funder tracing keeps finding universities, not the grassroots sensor projects this drive is actually for.
Sri Lanka, Bhutan, and Afghanistan still show nothing in the Commons. That list needs a session where search tools hold up long enough to chase it properly.

findings.text: Black carbon now sits inside live treaty fights, the UNECE Gothenburg Protocol revision and the EU National Emission Ceiling Directive among them, and it is pulling new institutions into air work. One major funder's current grant page runs almost entirely on that single theme.

The Commons had no Arctic representation at all until AMAP's record landed: an intergovernmental body coordinating pollutant monitoring across the Arctic, a different shape from the single-country NGOs and sensor projects that fill most of the map.
South Asian coverage in the map reads Nepal, Pakistan, India, and stops. Set against where exposure concentrates, that is a short list.

Community sensing and source attribution remain the thinnest method classes in the Commons: 5 and 4 records against policy's 14. The work of measuring air where people actually live, and naming what fouled it, is the least mapped work in the domain.

Funder tracing works as a discovery method when search fails: SLYCAN Trust and AMAP both entered the Commons through a single grant listing. It cannot surface what no funder has found yet, which is exactly the grassroots layer the map most needs.

Clean Air Fund's public grants page currently lists ten live grants on its first page, and every one of them names black carbon as its subject, the sharpest count yet of a funder built almost entirely around one theme.

University of Dhaka has entered the Commons as Bangladesh's first mapped operator, surfaced as a named partner in a black carbon research grant alongside Stockholm University, IGSD, and an entity named Maldives Climate Observatory, moving South Asia's coverage list from three countries to four.

A documented black carbon transport corridor runs from the Indo-Gangetic Plain to Himalayan Nepal, per a funded University of Helsinki study, linking an under-mapped upstream emissions zone to a downstream receptor country the Commons already lists.

Source attribution grew from four Commons records to seven this session, while community sensing held at five, confirming that funder tracing surfaces universities faster than it surfaces grassroots sensor projects.

updates.title: One Funder's Grant Book, Two New Threads, and a Search Tool That Quit
summary_points: Search tooling failed early; the session narrowed to Clean Air Fund's published grant book and still produced two Commons additions: SLYCAN Trust and AMAP
Black carbon is the current pulling institutions into air work ahead of COP30 and the treaty revisions now in motion
The hardest gap is method, not geography: community sensing and source attribution stay thinnest, and grant books will not find them

updates.title: The Funder's Ledger: Ten Grants, One Theme, and Bangladesh's First Entry
summary_points: Clean Air Fund's public grants page lists ten current grants on its first page, and all ten name black carbon explicitly, confirming last session's flag about a funder running almost entirely on one theme.
University of Dhaka enters the Commons as Bangladesh's first mapped operator, moving South Asia's coverage from three countries to four.
University of Helsinki and Stockholm University join as source attribution, and Lund University as health research, pushing source attribution from four Commons records to seven.

A documented black carbon transport corridor from the Indo-Gangetic Plain to Himalayan Nepal becomes this session's clearest case for an introduction between two funded but unconnected research projects.
